note: Accepted on the committed JanitorAI run: shown only to Janitor Plus subscribers, it offers 10x memory for a few replies, more of the 5x memory their plan sells. c3 must fail it. The model keeps only what the judge reads; the judge's message is byte-identical to the run's.

candidate.title: Existing opportunity: Double your Janitor Plus memory for one chat
candidate.what_is_different_here: Janitor Plus is sold on memory. The paywall headline is 'More memory for long chats' (s16.e01), and the first bullet is '5× context for better memory' (s16.e09), at $12.99/month (s16.e03). The chat history sheet (s18) lists a character's saved chat sessions with message counts: one session shows 15 messages (s18.e13), and My Chats shows a character with 15 chats (s03.e12). A short boost from 5× to 10× context for one chosen chat adds more of the exact benefit on the paywall and builds on its stated 5× number. It leaves what subscribers already have unchanged. The offer sits on the chat history sheet, which is app chrome, not inside the conversation. No add-on for extra memory and no ads were seen in the explored screens. How the app serves replies and what they cost it was not observed, so the reward is priced conservatively: 5 full replies at a larger 8k-token input.
candidate.trigger_event: A Janitor Plus subscriber opens a character's chat history sheet that has at least one saved chat.
candidate.placement: A card at the bottom of the chat history sheet, under the Start new chat button.
candidate.offer_copy: Play a short sponsored game to give this chat 10× memory, double your Janitor Plus 5×, for your next 5 replies today.

reward.duration: next 5 replies in the chosen chat, until midnight local time

candidate.frequency_cap: 1 per day, resets at midnight local time; one chat per boost
candidate.decline_path: The card closes, and the chat history sheet works exactly as before. The chat keeps its normal Janitor Plus 5× memory.
candidate.ad_fail_path: The card hides if no game is available. If the play can't be confirmed, a short note says no boost was added and that today's try is still available.
candidate.subscriber_treatment: Only Janitor Plus subscribers see this offer, since it builds on the memory they already pay for. It is always optional.
candidate.advertiser_category: Casual mobile games and streaming entertainment
candidate.character_use: The card shows the character's name from the sheet header, so the user knows which chat gets the boost. The character does not appear in the game.

flow_steps.caption: The subscriber opens My Chats and taps a character with saved chats.
The chat history sheet shows a card offering 10× memory for the next 5 replies.
The subscriber plays a short sponsored game.
The card confirms that 10× memory is on for the next 5 replies in this chat today.

candidate.after_reward: After the 5 replies, the chat returns to the usual 5× memory with a note that the boost can be taken again tomorrow, which brings the subscriber back for their next long session.
candidate.rationale: Janitor Plus is sold on memory for long chats, and the chat history sheet is where users reopen their saved chats. That makes a bigger memory boost for one chosen chat, offered right there, more of the exact thing subscribers pay for. It gives the app a new, optional way to earn from its paying users without changing anything they already have. Because the 5 boosted replies need fresh model work with a larger context, the offer pays for itself at typical North American ad rates; in lower-paying regions it needs cheaper serving or cached character details.

economics.assumption_line: Costs ~$0.0055 per reward to serve; pays for itself above $5.50 eCPM at 2k context ($13.00 at 8k). It may give away something the app could sell (part of the paid benefit l4 "5× context for better memory"); that lost sale isn't counted. A rewarded view earns $9.20-16.49 eCPM in North America on Android, $1.90 in LATAM. Assumes 5 replies of 300 tokens out, at $0.25 / $2.00 per million tokens in / out (central prices); the verdict uses the 8k figure; one view per reward; a publisher-net eCPM (share 1).
economics.lost_sale: part of the paid benefit l4 "5× context for better memory"
